hook: He used *Ray-Ban Meta* smart glasses, AI and a MacBook to cheat her at chess
caption:
♟️🤖 A guy just used Ray-Ban Meta glasses, AI, and a MacBook to cheat at chess, and his opponent had no idea.
Creator Sourgrape02 on TT challenged a woman to a game, claiming he had only played chess once or twice before.
What she didn't know was that his smart glasses were secretly feeding him the best moves.
Here's how it worked:
His Ray-Ban Meta glasses streamed the chessboard to a MacBook through a WhatsApp video call.
GPT tracked the pieces while Stockfish, one of the world's strongest chess engines, calculated the best moves.
The moves were sent back as audio through his glasses, allowing him to play without ever looking at a screen.
As the game went on, his opponent grew suspicious of how someone with so little experience could play so well.
The video ends with him winning by checkmate, though the edited footage doesn't show enough to verify the entire game.
It's an interesting look at how easily AI could change cheating in chess, poker, and other games played in person.
